content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E28","hypothesis_id":"H05","title":"TEA/TEOA matched catalytic readout with inert-gas, negative controls, and optional isotope follow-up","purpose":"Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution persists after tighter matching plus core controls, while limiting inference to a bounded donor comparison unless a platform-qualified substrate-associated signal is first established.","evidence_ids":["EV029","GX011","EV011","GX008"],"source_to_proposal":"EV011 supports the competing explanation that both TEA and TEOA can function through reductive quenching and donor-radical formation. EV029 and GX011 provide transferable, non-Co evidence that TEOA can participate in catalyst- or CO2-associated adduct chemistry beyond simple donation. GX008 supports inclusion of omitted-component controls, inert-gas comparison, and 13CO2 checks in homogeneous photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. Proposed transfer: in the researcher-stated Co(II)-bipyridine comparison platform, first establish whether a TEA/TEOA catalytic difference is reproducible under tightly matched conditions and core controls, then add one substrate-associated spectroscopic readout only if a pilot shows it is detectable and comparable in this platform. quantify CO and H2 for all groups and collect the same quenching readout for TEA and TEOA with identical blanks and references.","Only if a pilot demonstrates a detectable and repeatable substrate-associated or intermediate-associated signal in this platform, collect that signal for both donors under the same sample state and timing window.","If catalytic products exceed the laboratory detection threshold with acceptable repeatability, repeat the two catalytic groups under 13CO2 using the same analytical workflow.","Predefine comparison rules from replicate baseline data, including assay repeatability for quenching and minimum reportable product signals, before evaluating donor differences."],"measurements":["CO and H2 quantified together by one unchanged analytical method across all groups","Predefined quenching observable for the platform, such as emission quenching or excited-state decay of the light-absorbing component","If pilot-qualified, one substrate-associated or intermediate-associated spectral feature collected with matched blanks and backgrounds","For optional 13CO2 groups, isotopic product assignment if detectable","Covariates affecting comparability, including pH or apparent basicity proxy, optical density, visible precipitation, and color change","Replicate-to-replicate variability and practical detection limits for each readout"],"supports":"Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution under the matched donor comparison that remains after cobalt, dark, and inert-gas controls validate the assay, together with quenching observables that remain similar within a predeclared repeatability window and, if available, a donor-dependent substrate-associated or intermediate-associated signal. Consistent 13CO2 product origin would strengthen interpretation but would still not by itself establish a specific adduct structure.","refutes":"Evidence against H05 would be that the TEA/TEOA catalytic difference disappears under stricter matching, or that any remaining catalytic difference is accompanied by clearly different quenching behavior large enough to account for it, or that CO/H2 signals are reproduced in inert-gas, no-cobalt, or dark controls in ways that undermine a cobalt-linked donor-specific interpretation.","inconclusive":"Inconclusive if quenching and downstream-sensitive observables both change together, if the substrate-associated method cannot be qualified in this platform, if products are near detection limits, if isotope follow-up is below sensitivity, or if donor substitution changes bulk medium properties enough that multiple latent factors vary despite nominal matching.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent concentrations or irradiation settings. Use the researcher-stated Co-bpy baseline values only if explicitly verified in the supplied material; otherwise perform a pilot to define a workable window where both donors give measurable but not overloaded product signals and where the chosen quenching assay is above background. Operationalize 'similar quenching' before the main run as no donor difference larger than the empirically determined repeatability bound from replicate baseline measurements with the same assay and sample state. Add the substrate-associated module only if the pilot shows a reproducible signal in both donor conditions without uncontrolled precipitation or severe overlap.","limitations":"The card remains a staged discriminator because the supplied record does not establish a validated substrate-associated signal in the target platform. TEA and TEOA can alter several medium properties beyond donor identity, so even the primary donor contrast may combine donor, base, proton-management, and solvation effects. Inert-gas, no-cobalt, dark, and 13CO2 controls improve assignment but do not identify the exact active intermediate or prove a productive donor-catalyst adduct.","feasibility":"moderate"}]}
